root_idea.summary: No single unifying root principle is established in the supplied comparative evidence: the dominant lexical branch concerns coming and arriving, while a separate item denotes a place where water gathers.
root_idea.development: The coming branch extends from physical arrival and presence to the occurrence of events and the bringing or presentation of something. Quran-focused discussion also distinguishes actual arrival or attainment from mere intending.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole QAC group is the Quran-attested Form I verb; its public headword is normalized to the classical citation form جَاءَ.

senses.definition: To come, arrive, or be present; of an event, matter, time, command, or result, to come to pass or occur.
senses.usage_conditions: Used intransitively for real or figurative arrival. With a goal or recipient, it means to come to or reach; with مِنْ, to come from. The subject may be a person, thing, or abstract matter.

senses.definition: To bring, present, or produce a person, thing, proof, report, or other matter for someone or before an audience.
senses.usage_conditions: Commonly used with بِـ for the thing or person brought; the construction may describe bringing something along, presenting evidence, or producing a report or other matter.

senses.definition: To do, perform, execute, or effect something; also to utter or produce an act, saying, or novel expression.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with a direct object or with بِـ. In Quranic usage the construction can describe committing or producing an act rather than physically coming.

senses.definition: In the causative shape أَجَاءَ, to cause someone or something to come, or to compel or drive someone to resort to a place or thing.
senses.usage_conditions: This causative construction expresses being forced or driven to betake oneself somewhere, as in the Quranic account of the pangs of childbirth driving Mary to the palm-trunk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beget a child; of a woman, to give birth to a child.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive construction with بِـ, as in bringing forth a child.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a word or expression, to convey or import a meaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a meaning or interpretation as the object of what is conveyed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become or come to be in a particular state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A copular-like use in which the predicate describes the state into which something comes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Facing, fronting, or being opposite; also coinciding with someone in coming.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes being in front of or opposite another, or meeting and coinciding in the timing of arrival.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie with someone in frequency of coming and strive to surpass him in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic Form III use concerning repeated or competing arrival.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coming; the act or occurrence of coming.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun derived from جَاءَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A frequent comer; by extension, a frequent bringer of good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive descriptive form for someone characterized by frequent coming or bringing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where water gathers around a fortress or similar structure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate lexical item reported with the variant جِيِّئَةٌ.

cautions: The supplied QAC group reports all 278 tokens under the Form I identity and includes the surface form أَجَاءَ at 19:23, which the Classical lexical evidence identifies as a causative Form IV construction. That Quran-attested causative use is retained as a distinct sense because no separate QAC form group was supplied; this does not assert that أَجَاءَ is itself a Form I paradigm form.
